hook: Odd spikes on a duck-billed dinosaur's beak were blood vessel channels for a large keratin beak.
summary: Micro-CT scans of Tethyshadros show that features once read as beak spikes mark a network of nerves and vessels feeding a keratin sheath larger than the bone beneath. This suggests a sensitive, heat-exchanging beak used to crop gritty plants, like those of birds. Soft tissue is inferred from bone traces and bird comparisons in a single specimen, so the beak's size is an estimate.
title: The bird-like complexity of hadrosauroid beaks.
